content.content: 99	Trained $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure are \emph{jointly sufficient in tested configurations} for CIVO. Neither factor alone precedes pathological overestimation: trained embedding without multi-rate exposure (008a, 3 seeds, peak NVE $0.83$--$0.93\times$) and multi-rate exposure without embedding (008f, 3 seeds, peak NVE $\leq 1.41\times$) both remain below $1.5\times$. Cross-environment replication on Cheetah Run confirms generalization. Freezing the embedding (\texttt{requires\_grad=False}) dramatically reduces severity (NVE $0.19$--$1.88\times$ vs.\ trained $1.53$--$4.72\times$; 2/4 seeds below threshold, 2/4 transient self-correcting spikes; Table~\ref{tab:three_way_emb}); removing the embedding (008f) also avoids CIVO. A controlled three-way ablation varying \emph{only} embedding treatment (trained/frozen/removed, single seed; Table~\ref{tab:causal_ablation}) confirms that gradient training---not embedding presence---is necessary. Extending to additional seeds and environments, the onset rate remains 10/10 multi-joint locomotion runs (Fisher exact $p < 0.0001$ vs.\ 0/8 controls). Partial gradient blocking (exp\_044) does not prevent onset (peak NVE $4.45\times$) but permits delayed self-correction (final eval 538, 59\% baseline; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_factorial}), confirming that \emph{any} gradient pathway updating $e_{\dt}$ suffices to induce CIVO. Degradation scales monotonically with $\dt$ ($-47\%$ at $\dt{=}2$, $-81\%$ at $\dt{=}4$; Figure~\ref{fig:dt_amplification}).

This mitigation preserves the world model's ability to distinguish temporal scales (unlike embedding removal) while eliminating the imagination-side bias that drives value overestimation (Figure~\ref{fig:multiple_pathways}).
